topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the administrative opening, lecturer introduction, and learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and sources of mutation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the core concept of cancer as a clonal, genetic, and microenvironmental disease driven by endogenous processes, replication stress, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental exposure, bad luck, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the debate between intrinsic 'bad luck' and environmental mutagens in causing cancer, supported by global epidemiological and migration data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and mechanisms of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens and chronic infections, exemplified by Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma, contribute to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA damage through adducts, dimers, oxidative stress, and tissue-specific processes.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic concepts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic tumour promotion mechanisms, host developmental timing, and summarize the diverse factors governing carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for evaluating carcinogenicity and risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the experimental, genomic, epidemiological, and risk-benefit approaches used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
